thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Markets Continue To Retreat As Tech Stocks Get Hit Hard

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Markets Continue To Retreat As Tech Stocks Get Hit Hard
text:
By Dow Jones Newswires
Nikkei nears 1-month low; energy stocks also weigh down indexes
Asian stock markets were weak, though above session lows, in early trading Wednesday following the latest drubbing of U.S. stocks and oil futures.
Japan's Nikkei was down 0.6%, moving close to its lowest point in a month as energy and electronics stocks slid. Oil explorer Inpex (1605.TO) was down 3.7% while Sumitomo (8053.TO) , which has various natural-resource investments around the world, lost 3.4%. Meanwhile, Olympus (7733.TO) dropped an early 4.4% and Mitsubishi Electric (6503.TO) was off 3.3%. Nissan shares (NSANY) reversed a bit of yesterday's slide following the arrest of CEO Carlos Ghost.
Hong Kong stocks extended losses, with the Hang Seng Index off 0.3% after dropping more than 1% early on. While tech stocks lagged overall, Tencent (0700.HK) gained 1.4% and AAC (2018.HK) rose 1.1%. Oil company Cnooc (0883.HK) fell 3.5%.
In mainland China, the Shanghai Composite and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite were both down slightly. Energy stocks lagged after the latest plunge in oil prices Tuesday.
Sagging energy stocks also weighed down Australia's ASX 200 , with Woodside Petroleum (WPL.AU) down 2% and Santos (STO.AU) off 3.8%. New Zealand's benchmark was down slightly.
South Korea's Kospi declined 0.6%, as Samsung (005930.SE) dipped. Singapore's Strai Times Index rose 0.4% while Taiwan's Taiex slipped 0.3% as Apple (AAPL) suppliers Foxconn (2354.TW) and Largan Precision (3008.TW) fell.
(END) Dow Jones Newswires
